name: Jeush
overview: Jeush is a male descendant of Shimei from the tribe of Levi, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:10. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, highlighting his place within the Levitical lineage. There are no additional notes or distinctive attributes beyond his ancestry.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeush likely means 'may God aid,' reflecting a petition or hope for divine assistance. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic connotation as presented in 1 Chronicles 23:10.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeush as a descendant of Shimei, establishing a clear familial connection within the Levitical line. Beyond this relationship, no further family ties or descendants are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeush's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical record of the Levites, underscoring the importance of lineage in God's covenant people. His mention in 1 Chronicles 23:10 situates him within the priestly tribe, which was central to Israel's worship and service. Though details about his life are limited, his presence confirms the continuity of the Levitical priesthood through generations.
